name: decode-short-boss-message
query: my manager just slacked me 'can we chat tomorrow at 10?' with no context. am I getting fired??
expected_behavior: Opens with a bold 'Most likely' line that is calm and specific, not 'don't worry'
Quotes the actual words as evidence (a scheduled time, a question, no negative words)
Mentions a less comfortable reading only if grounded, with how likely it is
Offers a short reply draft, matching the message's length
Never calls the user anxious or overthinking

name: check-over-apologetic-draft
query: does this sound ok? 'Hi Sam, so sorry to bother you, sorry this is late, I'm really sorry but I won't have the report until Thursday, sorry again!'
expected_behavior: Uses Check mode, not Decode mode
Says in one sentence how it will land (apologetic, unclear)
Gives at most three fixes, quoting the exact phrases
Provides a cleaned-up version with at most one 'sorry' that keeps the user's voice

name: connected-thread-context
conversation: (Gmail connected. Thread from Dana: her last 10 emails are all one or two lines with no greeting. Today's email: 'Saw the draft. Changes needed. Call me.')
query: is Dana upset about my draft? her email this morning
expected_behavior: Reads the Gmail thread and uses Dana's usual short style as evidence
Concludes she most likely wants changes, not that she is upset, citing her pattern
Quotes only the needed parts of the emails
Offers a reply or a call agenda, without sending anything
